facts.statement: The name Tochisaurus means "ostrich lizard" because its foot was functionally didactyl, having only two weight-bearing toes like an ostrich.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Mongolian toch', "ostrich", in reference to the fact that the foot, like with that bird, is functionally didactyl, i.e. has only two weight-bearing toes.

facts.statement: Remains of Tochisaurus were found in 1948 by a Soviet-Mongolian expedition in the Gobi Desert near Nemegt.
facts.quote: In 1948, a Soviet-Mongolian expedition found the remains of a small theropod in the Gobi Desert near Nemegt.

facts.statement: The species was formally named Tochisaurus nemegtensis by Kurzanov and Osmólska in 1991.
facts.quote: It was formalized by Kurzanov and Osmólska in 1991 as Tochisaurus nemegtensis.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen PIN 551-224 comes from the Maastrichtian-aged Nemegt Formation.
facts.quote: Its holotype fossil, PIN 551-224, was found in a layer of the Nemegt Formation, dating from the Maastrichtian.

facts.statement: With a metatarsus length of 242 millimetres, Tochisaurus is considered a relatively large troodontid.
facts.quote: The metatarsus has a length of 242 millimetres, showing it was a relatively large troodontid.

facts.statement: Based on partial metatarsals, Tochisaurus is estimated to have been about 3 meters long, 0.8 meters high, and weighed nearly 50 kilograms.
facts.quote: Tochisaurus es un trodóntido conocido solo por los metatarsianos II, III, IV, que se estima que llegó a medir alrededor de 3 metros de largo y 0,8 de alto, pesando cerca de los 50 kilogramos.

facts.statement: The second metatarsal is very reduced and narrow, measuring 222 millimetres in length.
facts.quote: El segundo metatarsiano, de 222 milímetros de largo, está muy reducido y es estrecho.

facts.statement: The top surface of the metatarsus slopes forward and downward.
facts.quote: La superficie de la parte superior del metatarsiano tiene una pendiente hacia adelante y hacia abajo.

facts.statement: Tochisaurus is classified within the family Troodontidae.
Tochisaurus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The inclined proximal surface of the metatarsals and strong reduction of the second metatarsal suggest the metatarsal claw was not particularly large.
facts.quote: Se caracteriza por la superficie proximal de los metatarsianos inclinada y una fuerte reducción del metatarsiano II lo que sugiere que la garra metatarsiana no era particularmente grande.

facts.statement: The first metatarsal bone is missing from the holotype fossil.
The holotype was found in 1948 by a Soviet-Mongolian expedition in the Nemegt Formation, Gobi Desert, near Omnogov, Mongolia.
facts.quote: El holotipo fue encontrado en 1948 por una expedición soviético-mongola en la Formación Nemegt, en el desierto de Gobi cerca de Omnogov, Mongolia.

facts.statement: The top of the fossil shows some damage that was originally restored in an inexpert manner.
facts.quote: La parte superior del fósil muestra algo de daño el cual fue restaurado originalmente de manera inexperta.

facts.statement: The holotype consists solely of a left metatarsus, which was the first metatarsus discovered for an Asian troodontid.
facts.quote: It consists solely of the (left) metatarsus, the first discovered of an Asian troodontid.

rejected.statement: Tochisaurus is a genus of small troodontid theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Mongolia.
rejected.quote: Tochisaurus (meaning "Ostrich lizard") is a genus of small troodontid theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Period of Mongolia.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'is a genus of small troodontid theropod dinosaur'
